title: Kerala sees 21.69% rise in tax revenue in first half of financial year, non-tax receipts nearly double
content: Thiruvananthapuram: Kerala's tax revenue rose by 11,139 crore in the first half of the 2026-27 financial year, while non-tax revenue nearly doubled, even as concerns over borrowings and shortfalls in central grants persist. The state collected 62,506 crore in tax revenue between April and September, up 21.69% from 51,367 crore during the corresponding period last year, under the previous LDF government. Non-tax revenue increased from 5,968 crore to 10,263 crore, a rise of 4,295 crore. Expenditure on development projects also rose to 11,596 crore from 7,379 crore in the same period last year. However, the government has already utilised 63% of its planned borrowings for the financial year, raising concerns over its finances in the coming months. Against the budgeted 11,932 crore in central grants, Kerala has received only 505 crore so far, with no disbursements since July. Meanwhile, the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB) has mobilised 25,613 crore outside the government's guarantees. The Pension Company has raised 5,320 crore under a government guarantee to fund welfare pensions. Supplyco and the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) have borrowed 2,351 crore and 2,837 crore, respectively.
